Apple is reportedly working on a new option that will allow users to more thoroughly wipe the storage space on their iPhone when erasing the device — but there's a catch. Here's what we know.

China-Exclusive Feature

References found in the iOS 27.2 beta 1 code released today indicate that iPhones will gain a new erase option that will allow users to completely overwrite the device's entire storage space — including the inactive portions — with blank data.

In addition to erasing the iPhone's data, this feature will also overwrite the device's entire storage space — including inactive portions — with blank data. Apple warns users that this process may take longer than a standard erase and could affect the device's lifespan.

This is an interesting move, since currently when a user erases their iPhone, the device's encryption key is destroyed, rendering any remaining data effectively unreadable. Apple actually makes this clear in its Apple Platform Deployment support document:

After examining today's beta, 9to5Mac confirmed that in its current implementation, this feature will only apply to iPhone models sold in China — Apple appears to have added it to comply with upcoming data erasure regulations.

This is due to a new Chinese standard taking effect on January 1, 2027, which will require smartphones and other electronic devices to provide a more thorough method for wiping stored data, including overwriting.

For semiconductor storage (such as the flash storage used in smartphones), one approved method is to overwrite the user data in the storage space at least once with meaningless data. This aligns closely with what Apple describes as replacing the storage with blank data.

Finally, this new erase option won't be exclusive to the iPhone — code references also indicate it will support other devices, including iPad, HomePod, and Apple Vision Pro.
